flashcards.q: What did Basel I (1988) establish and its two flaws?
flashcards.a: Single global minimum: capital >= 8% of risk-weighted assets, with four buckets 0/20/50/100% keyed to OECD membership. Flaws: crude OECD-biased weights invited arbitrage; trading books untaxed until the 1996 Market Risk Amendment.

flashcards.q: Name the three pillars and what each contains.
flashcards.a: Pillar 1: minimum capital (credit SA/IRB, market VaR, operational). Pillar 2: supervisory review - ICAAP/SREP add-ons. Pillar 3: market discipline via disclosure. Crisis verdict: P1's models failed, P2 wasn't binding, P3 was unread.

flashcards.q: List the core Basel III capital numbers.
flashcards.a: CET1 >= 4.5%, +2.5% capital conservation buffer = 7% all-in; Tier1 6% (+buffer 8.5%); Total 8% (+10.5%); countercyclical buffer 0-2.5%; G-SIB surcharge 1-3.5%; leverage ratio >= 3% unweighted; TLAC 16%/18% RWA for GSIBs.

flashcards.q: Define LCR, key outflow assumptions, and HQLA caps.
flashcards.a: HQLA / 30-day stressed net outflows >= 100%. Outflows: stable retail 3-5%, less stable 10%, non-operational wholesale 40%. HQLA: Level 1 uncapped no haircut; Level 2A 15% haircut <= 40%; Level 2B <= 15%.

flashcards.q: NSFR formula and what it structurally prevents.
flashcards.a: Available Stable Funding / Required Stable Funding >= 100% over one year. ASF: capital 100%, retail deposits 90-95%, wholesale <6m 0-50%. RSF: cash 0%, Level1 5%, long loans ~85%. Prevents short-term wholesale funding of illiquid long assets.

flashcards.q: State the output-floor rule and phase-in schedules.
flashcards.a: Used RWA = max(internal-model RWA, 72.5% x total standardized RWA incl CVA). BCBS schedule: 50% in 2023 rising 5pp/yr to 72.5% by 2028; EU CRR3 started 2025 -> full effect 2030; US re-proposal targets completion ~2028. Caps model benefit at 27.5%.

flashcards.q: Revised standardized corporate and bank risk weights?
flashcards.a: Corporate: AAA-AA- 20%, A 50%, BBB 75%, BB-B 100%, <BB- or unrated 150%/100%. Banks ECRA: 20/30/50/100/150%. Retail flat 75%; past-due 150%; equity stakes 250%.

flashcards.q: What does IRB estimate and how did Basel IV constrain it?
flashcards.a: Bank models estimate PD/LGD/EAD/M feeding an ASRF 99.9% unexpected-loss capital formula (Foundation: supervisory LGD; Advanced: all internal). Basel IV added input floors - PD ~5bp mortgages/transactor retail, ~25bp other retail, LGD floors by collateral - because pre-crisis PDs near 0.03% were absurd.

flashcards.q: FRTB SA components vs IMM requirements - the delta.
flashcards.a: SA: sensitivities-based delta/vega/curvature with high/med/low correlation scenarios + Default Risk Charge + RRAO - mandatory everywhere. IMM: desk-level ES 97.5% with 10-120d liquidity horizons, gated by backtesting green zone and PLA (unresolved<10%). SA typically 1.3-2x IMM on flow desks; NMRF can flip exotics; output floor caps bank-wide edge at 27.5%.

flashcards.q: What is TLAC and why debt instead of more equity?
flashcards.a: G-SIB holding companies must hold eligible bail-in-able debt >= 16% (2022+: 18%) of RWA plus 6%/6.75% leverage-based TLAC so failures recapitalize without taxpayers. Debt beats equity on cost (tax-deductible, no dilution) while providing loss absorbency senior to equity but junior to operating claims.

flashcards.q: Which Basel-era gaps did SVB (2023) and Credit Suisse AT1s (2023) expose?
flashcards.a: SVB: exempt from LCR/NSFR (Category IV tailoring), ~90% uninsured deposits running in hours vs 30-day assumptions, HTM unrealized losses (~$15B+) outside capital marks. CS: CHF 16B AT1 written to zero while equity got UBS consideration - reversing expected seniority and freezing the AT1 market.

flashcards.q: Rank Basel I-IV by real-world impact and justify.
flashcards.a: III > I > IV > II. III reshaped funding/capital behavior permanently (buffers, LCR/NSFR, surcharges); I created the global metric; IV mid-flight (floors complete 2028-2030); II barely implemented where it mattered and discredited in 2008 though its pillar architecture persists.
